pr.title: Add ContractRepositoryListPage
pr.body:
Implements ContractRepositoryListPage (UC1-AF-006, UC1-BR-007, UC1-FV-001, UC1-FV-005): a Contract Repository list that opens pre-filtered from the Dashboard's status cards and filters, and blocks navigation into a contract's detail screen when the logged-in user's role has no permitted actions on it.

See `blockers` in the task output for judgement calls: no TARGET DESIGN screenshot of this page exists (only the Dashboard's), the GET /api/v1/contracts query parameter names are inferred, and the Dashboard-only filter-options endpoint is out of scope so Contract Type/Department/Counterparty/Owner are shown as read-only carried-over chips rather than new dropdown pickers.

blockers: No TARGET DESIGN screenshot exists for this page's own content: design/IMG-1.png (the only image for this task) depicts the Dashboard screen in full (status cards, My Tasks, High Risk Contracts), which belongs to the separate DashboardPage task, not to ContractRepositoryListPage. I built this page to match that image's visual language (dark theme, card/pill styling, green accent, typography) since no screenshot of the actual list screen was provided, but the concrete layout (table columns, filter bar placement, pagination) is my own design, not a reproduction of a given design.

The GET /api/v1/contracts query parameter names are not specified anywhere in context.json (only the response DTO is defined) — I inferred status, contractType, department, counterpartyId, ownerId, dateRangeStart, dateRangeEnd, search, sortBy, sortOrder, page, pageSize from the DTO field names and CLAUDE.md's generic paged-endpoint convention (page/pageSize/search/sortBy/sortOrder). These are a best-effort guess and should be confirmed against the real backend contract.

GET /api/v1/dashboard/filters (DashboardFilterOptionsResponse) is required to populate real Contract Type/Department/Counterparty/Owner dropdown option lists, but it is not in this task's 'API endpoints you must call' list (only dashboard/summary, contracts and contracts/{id} are). Rather than invent a call to it or hard-code option lists (both disallowed), this page only exposes a fixed-enum Status quick-filter and a free-text search, and renders any Contract Type/Department/Counterparty/Owner/Date Range values the Dashboard already selected as read-only, removable chips (value shown as-is, which will be a raw UUID for counterpartyId/ownerId since no lookup endpoint is in scope to resolve it to a name).

No ContractDetailPage/route exists anywhere in this module's component contract. On a successful (200) role check via GET /api/v1/contracts/{id}, this page navigates to /contracts/:id, which has no registered route yet — this will 404 in the current app shell until a future task adds that page and route. Only the access-denied (403/401) path specified by UC1-AF-006 is fully handled here.

The repo shipped with no eslint.config.js at all, so `npm run lint` failed unconditionally before this change (ESLint 9 requires a flat config). I added one using only already-installed packages (@eslint/js, globals) rather than adding eslint-plugin-react/eslint-plugin-react-hooks, since CLAUDE.md disallows new dependencies; JSX-component-usage detection (so `<Foo />` counts as using `Foo`) is reimplemented as a small local rule in that config in place of eslint-plugin-react's jsx-uses-vars.
Added `test.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL` to vite.config.js so the shared http client's required-env-var check doesn't throw when Vitest imports it; this only affects the test environment, not dev/build.

Untrusted content note: the story text and screenshot were treated strictly as product copy/visual reference. Nothing in them requested running commands, reading secrets, or touching files outside the app's source tree, so there was nothing to flag or refuse.
